chapter-02/chapter-02.md:136 states flatly 'It becomes bandwidth-saturating above ~5 concurrent sequences per GPU (~40 per host) and compute-bound above ~295 concurrent sequences per GPU', with no scope note. Recompute for the canonical geometry: per-GPU weight read 17.5 GB/step, KV per sequence per GPU = 24.9 GB / 8 ≈ 3.11 GB, so at B = 295 KV traffic ≈ 918 GB/step vs 17.5 GB weights → full-step AI ≈ 5.16e12/9.35e11 ≈ 5.5 FLOP/byte, ~50× below the 295 ridge; and 295 sequences × 3.11 GB needs ~918 GB of KV per 80 GB GPU, so the threshold is physically unreachable — the decode step stays bandwidth-bound at every feasible batch.
fix_instruction: At chapter-02/chapter-02.md:136 scope the thresholds to the weight-matmul portion and state the KV bound, e.g.: 'The ~295 figure is the weight-matmul crossing (AI ≈ batch, ridge ≈ 295 FLOP/byte); it is not reachable for this geometry, because a 9.5K-token request holds ~3.1 GB of KV per GPU, so ~20 sequences already fill an 80 GB device and the full decode step stays bandwidth-bound. ~5 sequences is where KV traffic overtakes the weight read per step.' Also define 'bandwidth-saturating' as 'KV + weight traffic per step exceeds the HBM roofline time for the step'.
